notes: מִלִּ → *at* / *At* checked as large-source-unit candidates: מִן and לְ are a compound of two prepositions rendered by one English word of which neither owns a part, so the pair fuses and heads on the first (rule 23); the alternative leaves לְ `unrepresented` beside מִן → *at*. פָּנֶה is not in the fusion because the ASV writes *the presence* for it (rule 30).

*thou* stands both after the imperative and before the vocative noun; the ASV's comma after *Tremble* sets it with *earth*, so it is read as the vocative's (rule 36), with the rule-17 reading as the competing one.
Supplied *the* before *Lord* and *God* belongs to those nouns (rules 15, 29); each *of* is the rectum's (rule 19).
